_meta.contract_note: THE DISCRIMINATOR (F80 mandate (2)): one field answers 'which contract is this' for every consumer, so a reader never has to guess from a filename or a shape. `sc-grammar.json` carries `contract = command-surface`. A tool handed the wrong file says so instead of finding no commands and reporting an empty grammar.
_meta.seeded: 2026-09-04, F80 -- generated by claude/harness/f80_ssgrammar.py from the loader census (claude/harness/f80_census.py). Hand-authored per key: the doc line, the value domain, the default and REQUIRED/optional, each read at the site the `source` array names. Mechanical: every anchor and every count.
_meta.anchor_pin: master-beta @ ba7a32a8 -- every `file:line` anchor in this file OUTSIDE `_meta` resolves at this commit. Gate: `anchor_gate` (ctest).
authority_chain: src/bodyModule/protosystem.cpp -- ProtoSystem::addBody, the LEGACY reader and the frozen comparison baseline (INTENT S11.52(b))
src/experimentalModule/ModularSystem.cpp -- ModularSystem::loadBody, the ONE composed authority (INTENT S11.78(d))
src/tools/ini_line.hpp -- the .ini LINE grammar for every reader but the legacy one (INTENT S11.115(b))
_meta.decisions: D16-D19 are RATIFIED, not proposed [vixy 2026-07-23, DECISIONS_PENDING.md:149-164 -> INTENT S11.79(j)-(m)]; D16 was ratified WITH AN OVERRIDE ('use type= instead of declare=') and the respell LANDED (INTENT S11.89, code f911646b): ONE `type=` key carries the declaration kind, `declare=` and `module=` are retired. The B28 'sign-off pending' state is DISCHARGED.
_meta.transitional: S11.89(c), the second veto point, VERBATIM: 'transitional body-type-under-`type=` on nodes (full `type=BODY` needs Tier-B emission beyond B25-emit's A1/A2)'. So a composed NODE today carries the legacy body type under `type=` (`type = Sun`), and `type = BODY` is the canonical marker for a body-type-less node. Moving every node to `type = BODY` is Vixy's decision, not a default -- and in a LEGACY file `BODY` is not a body type at all, which is why the legacy `type` domain below excludes it.
_meta.counts_note: Every count here is DERIVED by the generator from the census, never asserted. `seed_gate`'s ss half re-derives them from the data on every run.

tex_halo.why_no_reader: The halo texture. Every body in both corpora sets it; the only occurrences of the string in src/ are the two blocks that SYNTHESIZE a star from a catalogue object (protosystem.cpp:102, ssystem_factory.cpp:390), which write it and never read it back.

lighting.why_no_reader: Whether the body is lit. Same story as `tex_halo`, and the same two write sites (protosystem.cpp:105, ssystem_factory.cpp:393).

model3D.why_no_reader: A 3D model for the body. The one literal in src/ is `REP_MODEL3D` (spacecrafter.hpp:71), which is a DIRECTORY name -- app_settings.cpp:162 returns it with a '/' appended and call_system.cpp:130 lists it as a subdirectory. It is not a section key read. `model_name` is the key that does select a model.

ring_shadow.why_no_reader: Whether the rings cast a shadow. No occurrence in src/ at all.

sidereal_period.why_no_reader: No occurrence in src/ at all. `orbit_visualization_period` and `orbit_period` are the keys that exist.

tex_cloud.why_no_reader: A cloud-layer texture. No occurrence in src/ at all.

tex_cloud_normal.why_no_reader: A cloud-layer normal map. No occurrence in src/ at all.

_meta.dead_keys_note: PRESENT IN THE DATA, READ BY NOTHING -- the data-surface twin of INTENT S5.122. Measured 2026-09-04 over both legacy corpora: 189 lines of ~/.spacecrafter/ssystem.ini (8.2% of its key lines) and 164 of data/default_ssystem.ini (9.4%) reach no reader, and `tex_halo` and `lighting` alone are 180 of the field's 189 -- one of each on every body.

not_this_contract.system: galactic.ini -- names a stellar_systems/*.ini file for one system; read at ssystem_factory.cpp:736-737 inside loadSystem, whose params come from galactic.ini (opened at ssystem_factory.cpp:619). Not a body-section key.

neighbouring_grammars.galactic.ini: the system list: hip, name, system, x, y, z. Its x/y/z reach these loaders only as values written into a synthesized orbit map (ssystem_factory.cpp:334-336, :747-749), never read from a body section.
neighbouring_grammars.anchor.ini: the camera-anchor grammar (type = point|body|observatory|orbit), read by AnchorManager; it SHARES the barycenter orbit keys a/b/body_A/body_B through the same creator chain. B4's file, out of this contract's scope.
neighbouring_grammars.config.ini: moon_scale / sun_scale and the viewing mode; not a body file.

bool_legacy.doc: Legacy boolean. TRUE only for 'true' or '1' (any case); EVERY other value -- including 'on', 'yes' and a misspelling -- reads as FALSE, silently. There is no accepted FALSE set, so a typo is indistinguishable from a deliberate 'off'.

bool_composed.doc: Composed-path boolean. TRUE for 'true', 'on' or '1' (any case); every other value reads as FALSE, silently. NOTE it accepts 'on' where the legacy reader does not -- the same authored value can mean different things on the two paths.

double.doc: A number, parsed by std::stod: leading blanks are allowed and a trailing non-numeric tail is IGNORED ('12abc' reads as 12). Unparseable or absent falls back to the key's default.

string.doc: Taken verbatim, including any high bytes.

vec3f.doc: Three comma-separated numbers, 'r,g,b'. NB a space after a comma is not a separator the legacy positional reader forgives.

bool_suppress.doc: A module SUPPRESSION switch, and it reads the opposite way round from the other booleans: the module is on unless the key explicitly says 'false', 'off' or '0' (any case). Writing 'no' does NOT turn it off, and writing 'true' is the same as not writing the key at all.

int.doc: A whole number; an empty or unparseable value takes the key's default.

enum.doc: One of a fixed set the code enumerates; see the key's `domain`.

legacy.doc: `ssystem.ini` and `data/default_ssystem.ini`: the frozen field format. Selected by FILE LOCATION, never by sniffing content.
legacy.comment_rule: A '#' is a comment ONLY in column 0 (protosystem.cpp:134). A '#' anywhere else is read as part of the key or the value. The rest of the .ini family goes through tools/ini_line.hpp, which treats '#' as a comment ANYWHERE on the line (ini_line.hpp:16) -- so a mid-line '#' in a legacy file means different things to the two readers of that same file (the INTENT S5.39 class, on the comment axis).
legacy.line_rule: `key = value`, split at the first '='; the legacy reader uses substr(0,pos-1)/substr(pos+2), which assumes exactly ONE space each side of the '=' (protosystem.cpp:135-137). A line shorter than 2 bytes is skipped. Keys are CASE-SENSITIVE: no reader lowercases them.
legacy.section_rule: `[name]` opens a body section. A body is flushed when the NEXT header is seen, which is why the file ends with a `[end]` sentinel -- it is load-bearing and is not a body.
legacy.forbidden: New-format constructs must never be written into a legacy file: an older build must still read it (INTENT S2.0 D13, scedit C4).

composed.doc: `~/.spacecrafter/modularSystem/<Name>.ini`, the B24 format. The `.ini.disabled` twin is machine-owned and regenerated at every legacy load; adopting it means dropping the extension.
composed.comment_rule: A '#' starts a comment anywhere on the line (src/tools/ini_line.hpp:16).

section_kinds.module: A BodyModule attached to a node. Carries `body = <node>`, and its `type =` names the module FAMILY, not a body type. The presence of `body =` is the ONLY discriminator (src/experimentalModule/ModularSystem.cpp:1615-1626).

body_types.doc: The `type =` domain in a LEGACY section, and on a composed NODE.
body_types.matching: first four bytes; see the `type` key's notes

module_families.doc: The `type =` domain in a COMPOSED module section (one carrying `body =`). Also the default slot name of the module.
module_families.section_header: A module section's header is `[<node>:<slot>]`; the slot defaults to the family name, which is why the shipped twin reads `[Earth:MESH]`. The header is NOT what declares the family -- `type =` is.

coord_func.doc: The `coord_func =` domain: which orbit family positions the body.

a.doc: Weight of `body_A` in the barycentre split. `coord_func = barycenter` only.
a.notes: REQUIRED: an empty value drops the body (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:286-289). Only the RATIO is observable -- the position is body_A + (body_B - body_A) * b/(a+b) (orbit.cpp:1159) -- so a = b = 1 means the midpoint. Parsed by a BARE std::stod (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:304), not the guarded helper every other numeric key uses, so a non-empty non-numeric value throws out of the loader.

albedo.doc: How much light the surface reflects, 0..1.

apparent_magnitude.doc: Brightness parameter of a small body. THIS KEY AND `slope` TOGETHER gate the entire tail system: without both, no tail key on the body is read at all.
apparent_magnitude.notes: The setter it feeds is named setAbsoluteMagnitudeAndSlope (protosystem.cpp:840) while the key is spelled `apparent_` -- and `absolute_magnitude`, which the shipped file uses once, is read by nothing.

atmosphere_ambient_b.doc: Blue component of the atmosphere's ambient light.

atmosphere_ambient_deviation.doc: Angular spread of the ambient light, DEGREES.

atmosphere_ambient_g.doc: Green component of the atmosphere's ambient light.

atmosphere_ambient_r.doc: Red component of the atmosphere's ambient light.

atmosphere_ext_model.doc: File name of an external atmosphere table.

atmosphere_lim_inf.doc: Lower altitude bound of the atmosphere, METRES.

atmosphere_lim_landscape.doc: Altitude below which the landscape is drawn, METRES.

atmosphere_lim_sup.doc: Upper altitude bound of the atmosphere, METRES.

atmosphere_model.doc: Which built-in atmosphere model to use. An unrecognised value silently means NO model.

atmosphere_radius_factor.doc: Atmosphere radius as a multiple of the body's radius.

atmosphere_sun_deviation.doc: Angular spread of the sunlight through the atmosphere, DEGREES.

axial_tilt.doc: Extra tilt applied to the drawn body.

b.doc: Weight of `body_B` in the barycentre split. `coord_func = barycenter` only.

big_halo_size.doc: Size of the big halo. Only read when `tex_big_halo` is set.

binary_secondary.doc: Names the second body of an Earth-Moon-style barycentric pair.

body.doc: In a BodyModule section, the name of the node this module attaches to. Its PRESENCE is what makes a section a module declaration rather than a body.
body.notes: D16 RATIFIED. The `type=` disambiguator (ModularSystem.cpp:1615-1626). NEW-FORMAT ONLY (D13).

body_A.doc: English name of the first body of a barycentre pair -- the point the position is measured FROM. `coord_func = barycenter` only.
body_A.notes: REQUIRED: empty, or naming no loaded body, drops the body (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:291-302). The shipped anchor.ini states an intended rule the code does NOT enforce -- that `parent` and `body_A` should be the same body for the orbit to mean anything.

body_B.doc: English name of the second body of a barycentre pair -- the point the position is measured TOWARDS. `coord_func = barycenter` only.

bound_to_surface.notes: COMPOSED-PATH READ ONLY: the legacy loader never reads this key -- it derives the same state from `coord_func = location_orbit` (protosystem.cpp:598-609). Kept as an alias; prefer `relation`.

brightness.doc: Extra brightness applied to the body.

close_orbit.doc: Whether the orbit is drawn as a closed curve.
close_orbit.notes: LEGACY ONLY -- the composed loader's read is commented out (ModularSystem.cpp:1074).

compose.doc: Whether this body's modules are deduced from its keys or come only from explicit BodyModule declarations.

coord_func.doc: Which orbit family computes this body's position. Getting it wrong is not cosmetic: an unknown value means NO ORBIT, and the body is not added to the old render path at all.
coord_func.notes: Four values are intercepted before the creator chain (protosystem.cpp:561,575,594,598); three more are handled BY the chain (Bary -> Eliptic -> Comet -> Special, protosystem.cpp:65-68); the 32 `*_special` names are matched inside SpecialOrbit's constructor (orbit.cpp:770-901) and a body declaring one has EVERY orbital element IGNORED -- OrbitCreatorSpecial reads no key but this one. `surface_point` belongs to the experimental path only: the legacy reader names it in its own failure message as the one value it deliberately leaves to the other path (protosystem.cpp:636-645). NB the Callisto ephemeris is spelled `calisto_special`, with one 'l'.

ground_radius.doc: Radius the ground is drawn at, KILOMETRES.

halo.doc: Draw a halo around the body.
halo.notes: READ BY A DIFFERENT PREDICATE ON EACH PATH: strToBool (legacy, protosystem.cpp:685) vs isTrue (composed, ModularSystem.cpp:1243), so `halo = on` draws nothing on the old path and a halo on the new one.

halo_alpha_override.doc: Override the computed halo opacity. Read only together with `halo_scale_override`.

halo_scale_override.doc: Override the computed halo size. Read only together with `halo_alpha_override`.

hardcoded.doc: Marks a body the engine itself created, not the file.
hardcoded.notes: COMPOSED ONLY; a provenance marker, not authoring surface.

has_atmosphere.doc: Give this body an atmosphere. Presence of this key OR of `atmosphere_lim_landscape` is what opens the whole atmosphere block.

hidden.doc: Load the body but do not show it.
hidden.notes: Same two-predicate split as `halo` (protosystem.cpp:983 vs ModularSystem.cpp:1400).

hint.doc: Draw the body's hint marker. On unless you turn it off.

label_color.doc: Colour of the body's name label.

light_source.doc: Declares that this body EMITS light. In a legacy file the same fact is inferred from `type`; in a composed file it must be stated.

model_name.doc: Name of the 3D model to draw instead of a sphere.

name.doc: The body's English name. THIS IS THE IDENTITY: it must be unique across every loaded system, and a second body with the same name is refused, not merged. Without it the section is skipped entirely.
name.notes: D34/S11.109(c). Both loaders refuse a duplicate AND SAY SO at L_WARNING (protosystem.cpp:546-549, ModularSystem.cpp:1057-1060) -- the drop is logged, not silent, which scedit INTENT C4's wording predates.

oort.doc: Make this body an Oort cloud.

oort_elements.doc: How many particles the Oort cloud draws.

orbit.doc: Draw the body's orbit line. On unless you turn it off.

orbit_alt_end.doc: Altitude the body finishes its ascent at, KILOMETRES. One of the three ascent keys, and all three must be given together.
orbit_alt_end.notes: D19 RATIFIED [vixy 2026-07-23 -> INTENT S11.79(m)]. src/experimentalModule/orbitModules/SurfacePointOrbitLoader.hpp:148-154; `coord_func = surface_point`, which the legacy path does not have.

orbit_argofpericenter.doc: Direction of closest approach, measured from the ascending node, DEGREES. `comet_orbit` only.
orbit_argofpericenter.notes: NOT interchangeable with `ell_orbit`'s `orbit_longofpericenter`: the two differ by the ascending node (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:85 vs :219). Copying a value between an ell_orbit and a comet_orbit section under the obviously corresponding name is wrong by that angle.

orbit_ascendingnode.doc: Where the orbit crosses the reference plane going north, DEGREES.

orbit_ascent_duration.doc: How long the ascent lasts, DAYS. One of the three ascent keys.

orbit_ascent_start.doc: Julian day the ascent begins. One of the three ascent keys.

orbit_bounding_radius.doc: Radius used for visibility/bounding tests, when the orbit cannot supply one.
orbit_bounding_radius.notes: For `ell_orbit` the value is OVERWRITTEN by the orbit's own computed radius (protosystem.cpp:647-649), so authoring it there has no effect. Composed read is commented out (:1075).

orbit_eccentricity.doc: How elongated the orbit is; 0 is a circle.

orbit_epoch.doc: Julian day the orbital elements are given at.

orbit_inclination.doc: Tilt of the orbit plane, DEGREES.

orbit_lat.doc: Latitude on the parent's surface, DEGREES.

orbit_lon.doc: Longitude on the parent's surface, DEGREES.

orbit_longofpericenter.doc: Direction of closest approach, measured from the reference direction, DEGREES. `ell_orbit` only.
orbit_longofpericenter.notes: See `orbit_argofpericenter` -- the comet spelling is a DIFFERENT angle.

orbit_meananomaly.doc: Where the body is on its orbit at the epoch, measured from pericentre, DEGREES. `comet_orbit` only.
orbit_meananomaly.notes: Required TOGETHER with `orbit_epoch` when `orbit_timeatpericenter` is absent (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:207-210).

orbit_meanlongitude.doc: Where the body is on its orbit at the epoch, measured from the reference direction, DEGREES. `ell_orbit` only.
orbit_meanlongitude.notes: Offset from `comet_orbit`'s `orbit_meananomaly` by the longitude of pericentre (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:86).

orbit_meanmotion.doc: How fast the body goes round, DEGREES PER DAY. `comet_orbit` only; an alternative to `orbit_period`, and it wins when both are present.

orbit_pericenterdistance.doc: Closest approach distance, ASTRONOMICAL UNITS. `comet_orbit` only.
orbit_pericenterdistance.notes: Required unless `orbit_semimajoraxis` is given. The absence test is `<= 0.0` (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:158), so an explicit 0 is indistinguishable from not writing the key.

orbit_period.doc: Time the body takes to go once round its parent, DAYS.
orbit_period.default: 0 under ell_orbit; treated as absent under comet_orbit
orbit_period.notes: Under `ell_orbit` an ABSENT period is not an error: it defaults to 0 and the orbit then divides by it (orbit.cpp:450,569), so the body gets an infinite or NaN mean anomaly silently. Under `comet_orbit` it is required only when the parent body itself has a parent (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:182-186). It is ALSO the fallback for `rot_periode`, so editing it changes how fast the body SPINS unless `rot_periode` is present (protosystem.cpp:960).

orbit_semimajoraxis.doc: Half the orbit's long axis. THE UNIT DEPENDS ON `coord_func`: KILOMETRES under `ell_orbit`, ASTRONOMICAL UNITS under `comet_orbit`.
orbit_semimajoraxis.default: 0 under ell_orbit; treated as absent under comet_orbit
orbit_semimajoraxis.notes: One key, one file, two units a factor of 1.496e8 apart: orbit_creator_cor.cpp:78 divides by AU, orbit_creator_cor.cpp:159 does not. The composed loaders reproduce the asymmetry (ElipticOrbitLoader.hpp divides, CometOrbitLoader.hpp does not), so it is the data grammar and not a one-path defect. Under `comet_orbit` it is REQUIRED unless `orbit_pericenterdistance` is given (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:158-164).

orbit_timeatpericenter.doc: Julian day of a pericentre passage. `comet_orbit` only, and the alternative to giving `orbit_epoch` + `orbit_meananomaly`.

orbit_visualization_period.doc: Period used when drawing the orbit curve, days.

orbit_x.doc: Fixed position, X, for a body that does not move.

orbit_y.doc: Fixed position, Y, for a body that does not move.

orbit_z.doc: Fixed position, Z, for a body that does not move.

parent.doc: The English name of the body this one orbits. 'none' makes it the centre of its system. Absent is NOT the same as 'none': it warns and adopts the centre body anyway. A name that names nothing skips the body.
parent.default: the centre body, with a warning
parent.notes: Order matters: a parent must appear EARLIER in the file (ModularSystem.cpp:773-778 resolves by name against what is loaded).

parent_rot_J2000_longitude.doc: The parent's J2000 longitude, in RADIANS, used only when `parent` names nothing that exists.

parent_rot_asc_node.doc: The parent's ascending node, in RADIANS, used only when `parent` names nothing that exists.

parent_rot_obliquity.doc: The parent's obliquity, in RADIANS, used only when `parent` names nothing that exists.
parent_rot_obliquity.notes: RADIANS, not degrees -- every `orbit_*` angle in the same section is degrees, these three are not (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:50,125 apply no conversion; the writer at orbit.cpp:608 emits them raw while orbit.cpp:597 converts `orbit_inclination`). IGNORED whenever `parent` resolves: the values then come from the parent body itself, so editing this on a body with a real parent changes nothing and says nothing (orbit_creator_cor.cpp:49,124).

path.doc: Directory the big-halo texture is looked up in.

planet_grid.doc: Draw a coordinate grid on this body.
planet_grid.notes: COMPOSED ONLY; installs a CUSTOM module in the named GRID slot.

primary.doc: Declares this body the primary star of its system.

radius.doc: The body's radius in KILOMETRES. Absent reads as 0, which is a body with no size rather than an error.

relation.doc: How this body is attached to its parent. Supersedes `bound_to_surface`, and is the only way to reach 'inner' from a file.
relation.notes: D16 RATIFIED [vixy 2026-07-23, S11.79(j)]. NEW-FORMAT ONLY: writing it into a legacy file breaks downgrade (D13). Declaring it AND a disagreeing bound_to_surface is a diagnosed conflict, explicit wins (ModularSystem.cpp:1301-1310).

replace.doc: Allow this section to REPLACE an already-loaded body of the same name instead of being skipped.

ring_shadow_color.doc: How much light of each channel survives the ring's shadow, 'r,g,b'.
ring_shadow_color.notes: src/experimentalModule/moduleLoader/RingLoader.cpp:35-37. NB the LEGACY-looking spelling `ring_shadow` that both corpora carry is NOT this key and is read by nothing.

rings.doc: Give this body a ring system. The three ring keys are only read when this is true.

rot_epoch.doc: Julian day the rotation angles are measured at.

rot_equator_ascending_node.doc: Where the body's equator crosses the parent's, DEGREES.

rot_frame.doc: Which frame the rotation keys above are authored in. Absent, it is DERIVED: pole keys present means absolute, otherwise parent-relative.
rot_frame.default: derived from which rotation keys are present
rot_frame.notes: COMPOSED ONLY. An invalid value falls back to the derived default with an actionable diagnostic (ModularSystem.cpp:944-952).

rot_obliquity.doc: Tilt of the body's equator relative to its PARENT's equator, DEGREES.

rot_periode.doc: How long the body takes to turn once, in HOURS.
rot_periode.notes: The 24-hour fallback is an ACTING DEFAULT: the composed loader logs it (ModularSystem.cpp:1342-1350, D12), the legacy loader does not (protosystem.cpp:960).

rot_pole_de.doc: Declination of the body's north pole, absolute J2000, DEGREES. See `rot_pole_ra`.

rot_pole_ra.doc: Right ascension of the body's north pole in the ABSOLUTE J2000 frame, DEGREES. Writing either pole key switches the whole orientation to the absolute frame and REPLACES rot_obliquity/rot_equator_ascending_node.

rot_pole_w0.doc: IAU prime meridian W0 for an absolute-pole body, DEGREES; converted by the loader into the internal referential.

rot_precession_rate.doc: Rate the rotation axis precesses, degrees per Julian century.

rot_rotation_offset.doc: Prime-meridian angle at the epoch, DEGREES.

shadow_color.doc: How much light of each channel survives this body's shadow, 'r,g,b'.

shadow_exempt.doc: Declares that this body neither casts nor receives shadows.

sidereal_time.doc: Which sidereal-time model drives the body's rotation phase.

slope.doc: Brightness slope parameter of a small body. See `apparent_magnitude`.

slot.doc: Name of the slot a module is installed into, when a body carries more than one module of a family.

sol_local_day.doc: Length of the body's solar day, in the units the body's own day is counted in.

surface_model.doc: Which lighting lineage the surface uses. In a legacy file it is inferred from `type = Moon`.

system_star.doc: Declares this body the star that defines the system.

tail.doc: Give a comet its tail. On for a comet that has the magnitude keys, unless turned off; `tail = true` forces it on for a body that is not a comet.
tail.default: on for a comet with magnitude keys
tail.notes: src/experimentalModule/ModularBody.cpp:875-876 -- the one switch read BOTH ways: not-false to keep the deduced answer, and explicitly true to override it.

tex_big_halo.doc: Texture for the large halo drawn around a star. Setting it is what ENABLES the big halo.

trail_color.doc: Colour of the trail the body leaves.

trail_length.doc: How many samples of trail the body keeps.
trail_length.default: from `type` (legacy: Planet/Dwarf 1460, Comet 2920, else the default)

type.doc: What the body IS -- the body class. Drives which object is built and, in a legacy file, a set of capabilities that the composed format states as keys of their own. An unrecognised value falls back to 'Asteroid' WITH a warning.
type.notes: MATCHED ON THE FIRST FOUR BYTES (protosystem.cpp:477-501): `casify` packs 4 bytes and the switch compares them, so any value sharing a 4-byte prefix with a canonical name is ACCEPTED -- 'Planetoid' loads as Planet, 'Moonlet' as Moon. A value shorter than 3 bytes is UNKNOWN. The 3-byte names ('Sun', 'KBO') match exactly, their 4th byte being the terminator. The composed loader does NOT share this: it compares the whole string (ModularSystem.cpp:1103,1113), so 'Moonlet' is a Moon to the old path and not a Moon to the new one.
